UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile information within the Codex Teams application. This entity stores non-authentication-related user data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

email.description: The user's email address, used for identification but not for authentication storage.

avatarUrl.description: URL to the user's profile picture or avatar.

workspaceIds.description: References to Workspaces the user is a member of. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N Workspace)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

Workspace.title: Workspace
Workspace.description: Represents a collaborative workspace where users can interact, create channels, and send messages.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Workspace entity.

description.description: A brief description of the workspace.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the workspace was created.

ownerId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who owns this workspace. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Workspace)

memberIds.description: References to UserProfiles who are members of this workspace. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N Workspace)

Conversation.title: Conversation
Conversation.description: Represents a discussion context, which can be a public/private channel or a direct message conversation between users.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Conversation entity.

type.description: The type of conversation (e.g., 'channel' for multi-user discussions, 'directMessage' for 1:1 chats).

name.description: The name of the conversation (e.g., 'General' for a channel, or a concatenated name for DMs).

workspaceId.description: Reference to the Workspace this conversation belongs to. (Relationship: Workspace 1:N Conversation)

memberIds.description: References to UserProfiles participating in this conversation. For direct messages, this array will contain exactly two IDs. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N Conversation)

isPrivate.description: Indicates if the conversation is private (true for private channels and direct messages, false for public channels).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the conversation was created.

lastMessageId.description: Optional reference to the ID of the most recent message in this conversation, for quick display. (Relationship: Message 1:1 Conversation)

Message.title: Message
Message.description: Represents an individual message sent within a conversation, supporting rich text formatting.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Message entity.

conversationId.description: Reference to the Conversation this message belongs to. (Relationship: Conversation 1:N Message)

senderId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who sent this message. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Message)

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the message was sent.

content.description: The plain text content of the message.

richTextContent.description: The rich text formatted content of the message, stored as a string (e.g., JSON representation of a rich text editor's output).

mentionsUserIds.description: Optional references to UserProfiles mentioned in the message. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N Message)

isEdited.description: Flag indicating if the message has been edited.

editedAt.description: Timestamp when the message was last edited, if 'isEdited' is true.

Summary.title: Summary
Summary.description: Represents an AI-generated summary of a conversation or a segment of messages within it.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Summary entity.

conversationId.description: Reference to the Conversation that was summarized. (Relationship: Conversation 1:N Summary)

summarizedByUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who initiated the summary generation, if applicable. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Summary)

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the summary was generated.

startMessageId.description: Optional reference to the first Message in the summarized thread/activity. (Relationship: Message 1:N Summary)

endMessageId.description: Optional reference to the last Message in the summarized thread/activity. (Relationship: Message 1:N Summary)

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore structure for Codex Teams prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence through extensive denormalization.

**Authorization Independence (No `get()` calls in rules):**
This is achieved by denormalizing crucial authorization context from parent and grandparent documents into their subcollections. Specifically:

1.  **Workspaces (`/workspaces/{workspaceId}`):** Each `Workspace` document directly contains `ownerId` and `memberIds`. This allows rules to check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId || request.auth.uid in resource.data.memberIds` for direct access to the workspace itself, without needing to `get()` any other document.

2.  **Conversations (`/workspaces/{workspaceId}/conversations/{conversationId}`):** Each `Conversation` document will denormalize `workspaceOwnerId` (from its parent `Workspace.ownerId`) and `workspaceMemberIds` (from its parent `Workspace.memberIds`). Combined with its existing `memberIds` (conversation-specific members) and `isPrivate` flag, a `Conversation` document contains all information needed to determine access. Rules can then evaluate `request.auth.uid in resource.data.memberIds` (for private conversations) or `request.auth.uid in resource.data.workspaceMemberIds` (for public conversations), eliminating `get()` calls to the parent workspace.

3.  **Messages (`/workspaces/{workspaceId}/conversations/{conversationId}/messages/{messageId}`):** Each `Message` document will denormalize `workspaceId`, `conversationId`, `conversationMemberIds` (from its parent `Conversation.memberIds`), `conversationIsPrivate` (from its parent `Conversation.isPrivate`), `workspaceMemberIds` (from its grandparent `Workspace.memberIds`), and `conversationWorkspaceOwnerId` (from its grandparent `Workspace.ownerId`). This ensures that a `Message` document is entirely self-sufficient for authorization, making rules simple and efficient without any `get()` operations.

4.  **Summaries (`/workspaces/{workspaceId}/conversations/{conversationId}/summaries/{summaryId}`):** Similar to `Message` documents, each `Summary` document will carry the same denormalized authorization fields (`workspaceId`, `conversationId`, `conversationMemberIds`, `conversationIsPrivate`, `workspaceMemberIds`, `conversationWorkspaceOwnerId`) to achieve complete authorization independence from its parent and grandparent documents.

**Querying for Access Patterns (QAPs):**

The structural segregation and denormalization enable robust QAPs:

*   **User Profiles (`/userProfiles/{userId}`):** Primarily accessed directly by the user, not typically listed globally. When needed, `get('/userProfiles/' + request.auth.uid)` is secure.
*   **Workspaces (`/workspaces/{workspaceId}`):** Users can efficiently list all workspaces they are members of using a `where('memberIds', 'array-contains', request.auth.uid)` query. This query is performant and secure because the `memberIds` array is directly on the `Workspace` document, making its security posture homogeneous.
*   **Conversations (`/workspaces/{workspaceId}/conversations/{conversationId}`):** Within a specific workspace, a user can query for conversations they have access to. For private conversations, `where('memberIds', 'array-contains', request.auth.uid)` is used. For public conversations within that workspace, `where('workspaceMemberIds', 'array-contains', request.auth.uid)` can be used alongside a filter for `isPrivate == false`. The combination of denormalized fields makes these `list` operations secure and efficient, as rules can validate based on the queried documents' own data.
*   **Messages & Summaries (`/workspaces/{workspaceId}/conversations/{conversationId}/messages/{messageId}` and `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/conversations/{conversationId}/summaries/{summaryId}`):** Listing messages or summaries within a specific conversation is secure. The denormalized fields (`conversationMemberIds`, `conversationIsPrivate`, `workspaceMemberIds`) in each message/summary document allow security rules to verify that the requesting user has access to the conversation context without requiring any additional `get()` calls. The client-side query simply requests the messages, and the rules enforce the authorization on each returned document.

This design avoids the pitfalls of hierarchical authorization, provides clear intent for security rules, and supports atomic operations and efficient queries, aligning with all specified design principles and mandates.
